tools.name: show_flight_options
tools.title: Show flight options
tools.description: Searches flights and returns them as an interactive A2UI surface the user can pick from, instead of a list of text. This is the answer whenever the turn is about flying — "show me flights", "what's the cheapest", picking an outbound or a way home — and it is the answer even if some detail of the trip is still soft. Do not redraw the trip panel instead: that asks again for dates they have already given and shows no fares.

origin.description: Departure airport code. Required — the trip is not priced without one.

surface.description: Where this surface will be placed. 'inline' (default) answers the current message; 'sidebar' is a persistent panel of controls; 'home' is a standing summary. It changes what is composed, not just where it goes.

tools.name: show_hotel_options
tools.title: Show places to stay
tools.description: Searches stays and returns them as A2UI hotel cards with rating, neighbourhood and nightly rate. This is the answer whenever the turn is about where to sleep — "find me a hotel", "somewhere near the Prado", comparing neighbourhoods. Do not redraw the trip panel instead.

surface.description: Where this surface will be placed. 'inline' (default) answers the current message; 'sidebar' is a persistent panel of controls; 'home' is a standing summary. It changes what is composed, not just where it goes.

tools.name: show_trip_controls
tools.title: Show trip controls (sidebar)
tools.description: Returns the trip panel: controls for the trip's own boundaries — dates, party size, budget, stop preference — with one commit action, pre-filled from whatever is already decided. Use it for the boundaries and nothing else. Somebody who has just said where they want to go and roughly when has not given you their dates or the airport they leave from, so record what they did tell you and call this in the same turn; asking out loud instead — "what dates did you have in mind?" — leaves them repeating a date you had a control for. Also for "move it a week later" or "make it three of us". Once the boundaries are settled, stop drawing it. Every step after them has its own tool, and that tool is the answer: flights are show_flight_options, stays are show_hotel_options, days are show_itinerary, the total is show_price_summary. Drawing this panel again at somebody who asked for flights shows them the dates they already gave you and no flights at all. The panel replaces itself each time; it is not a feed.

tools.name: show_itinerary
tools.title: Show a day-by-day itinerary
tools.description: Builds a day-by-day plan for a destination from its real highlights and returns it as an A2UI itinerary the user can tap through.

tools.name: show_trip_dashboard
tools.title: Show a trip dashboard
tools.description: Returns a generated dashboard for a trip: days remaining, budget used, forecast and a map of what is planned. Use for "how is my trip looking" questions.

tools.name: show_price_summary
tools.title: Show what a trip costs
tools.description: Returns an itemised cost breakdown and total as an A2UI price summary.
